title: Christ the Lamb takes away the world's sins
source_text: IV. Quoniam autem Deus tantum beneficium nobis confert per & propter Christum, idcirco dicitur a Joanne Baptista, Agnus Dei qui tollit peccata mundi. Joan. 1. Quo spectat alter Joannes, dum ait in prima epistola, Scitis quia ille apparuit, ut peccata nostra tolleret. Et Apostolus Paulus in epistola ad Hebraeos docens Christum apparuisse sine peccato ad destituitionem, sive abolitionem peccati; & illum semel oblatum fuisse ad exhaurienda, sive tollenda multorum peccata.
pass_a_gloss: But since God confers so great a benefit on us through and on account of Christ, therefore he is called by John the Baptist the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world (John 1). To which the other John looks when he says in the first epistle, You know that he appeared that he might take away our sins. And the Apostle Paul in the epistle to the Hebrews teaching that Christ appeared without sin for the destitution, or abolition, of sin; and that he was offered once to exhaust, or take away, the sins of many.
pass_b_english: John the Baptist calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sins (John 1).
1 John and Hebrews teach he appeared and was offered once to abolish many's sins.
